unactioned_insights.title: Autoscaling cluster with Spark dynamic allocation disabled causes executor eviction and task failures
unactioned_insights.description: The Databricks cluster is configured for autoscaling (min=1, max=14 workers) but `spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled` is explicitly false. The VM-layer autoscaler scales workers up and down without Spark's knowledge, so when the autoscaler removes a node it kills the executor mid-task rather than letting Spark drain it gracefully. This explains the 124 task failures, 203 task retries, and 5 stage failures observed in this run — executor removal events for executors 0–5 show `cause: kill request from HTTP endpoint`, confirming forced eviction. vcore utilization is 43.4% and cpu_efficiency is 44.3%, indicating substantial idle capacity caused by Spark not being able to request executors on-demand.
unactioned_insights.reason: planner hit its iteration budget before producing recommendations

unactioned_insights.title: Structural ~60 GB disk spill on every run — shuffle partitions too coarse for data volume
unactioned_insights.description: Every one of the 20 historical runs spills 60–64 GB to disk (trend: STABLE, mean=62.6 GB, std=1.37 GB). This is not a transient event; it is a fixed structural characteristic of the current configuration. With 11 TB of shuffle written per run and only 400 static shuffle partitions, each partition carries ~27 GB of shuffle data on average. Executor off-heap memory is 74 GB total but shared across 16 concurrent tasks, leaving ~4.6 GB per task — far below the per-partition shuffle size. AQE is not active (spark.sql.adaptive.enabled is not set), so no runtime coalescing is occurring. Increasing shuffle partitions would distribute shuffle data across more, smaller partitions, each fitting comfortably in executor memory and eliminating the spill.
unactioned_insights.reason: planner hit its iteration budget before producing recommendations

unactioned_insights.title: Legacy stop-the-world GC collector (PS MarkSweep) with gradual GC time increase trend
unactioned_insights.description: All executors are running with the Parallel Scavenge + PS MarkSweep GC combination — a fully stop-the-world collector on Java 8 (confirmed by java.version=1.8.0_482). Cumulative executor GC time has increased 7.4% over 20 runs (from 3,194s to 3,431s, trend_direction=INCREASING) even though data volume is stable. This gradual degradation suggests heap fragmentation accumulating over the executor JVM lifetime. PS MarkSweep performs full stop-the-world pauses that block all 16 executor tasks simultaneously, making GC pauses disproportionately costly on these 16-core executors. Switching to G1GC would provide concurrent collection and bounded pause times.

unactioned_insights.description: This run completed in 20,403s versus a historical mean of 29,263s (z-score=-6.88, percentile=0, band=anomalously_low). agent_insights.description: All executors are running with the Parallel Scavenge + PS MarkSweep GC combination — a fully stop-the-world collector on Java 8 (confirmed by java.version=1.8.0_482). Cumulative executor GC time has increased 7.4% over 20 runs (from 3,194s to 3,431s, trend_direction=INCREASING) even though data volume is stable.
